summary: The skills are mostly careful about the main guardrails: evidence before Done, no gate closed by an agent, screening pasted input, and treating pasted text as data. The main gaps are elsewhere. The shell hook is easy to bypass. The review flow can send artifacts to a backend that wasn't approved, and its default backend can't produce a valid round. Several skills assume Cloud SQL, a known 14-to-18 target, or a skill that doesn't exist (decision record, logical runbook). Catch-up depends on bootstrap steps that bootstrap's own guard blocks.

findings.claim: The shell guard only matches a rule when the forbidden program starts the segment. Global flags before the subcommand, or wrapping the command in sh -c or bash -c, get past it, including a production MVU patch, terraform apply and a push to main. The skills and the SOP lean on this hook as the backstop for 'people run provider commands'.
findings.evidence: Line 181: 'if (rule.test.test(prog) && rule.test.exec(prog)?.index === 0) deny(...)'. Line 91 regex starts '\bgcloud\s+(?:beta\s+|alpha\s+)?sql\s+'. When run locally, the hook returned allow for 'gcloud --project=p sql instances patch prod --database-version=POSTGRES_18', 'bash -c "gcloud sql instances patch prod ..."', 'bash -c "psql -h prod.db.internal -c select"', 'sh -c "terraform apply -auto-approve"', 'git -C repo push origin main', and the kit's raw 'curl -X POST https://sqladmin.googleapis.com/.../preCheckMajorVersionUpgrade'. sop.md section 7 says the guardrails 'are enforced by the plugin's rules and hook'.
findings.suggested_fix: Recurse into sh -c, bash -c, eval and xargs payloads, and let gcloud, git and gh global flags appear before the subcommand. Add deny rules for sqladmin.googleapis.com and other provider REST endpoints, and add these cases to the evals.

findings.claim: Nothing ties the reviewers list to approvedReviewBackends. The round script defaults to a Codex/OpenAI reviewer, and /pg-review tells the agent to pick any three models when project.json lists none. Customer artifacts can reach a provider the program owner never approved.
findings.evidence: run-review-round.sh line 18: 'reviewers="${REVIEWERS:-codex:gpt-6-astra cursor:gemini-4-argon-high ...}"'. commands/pg-review.md line 8: 'If none are listed there, use three available models from different families.' pg-upgrade-model-review SKILL.md line 18: 'Use only the backends listed in approvedReviewBackends. If it's missing, use subagent only.' Line 12: 'Reviews send the artifacts to model providers', but line 18 only asks before 'any backend outside Cursor'.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the script refuse to run without an explicit REVIEWERS value, and have the skill drop any reviewers entry whose backend isn't in approvedReviewBackends. Fix /pg-review to fall back only to approved backends, and treat every external model provider, not only non-Cursor backends, as covered by the regulated-data check.

findings.claim: The default and only pre-approved backend is 'subagent', but the reviewer agent is model: inherit. The skill never says how to give subagents different models, so a default round has one model family and fails the skill's own two-family rule. The skill also tells the agent to check availability with cursor-agent --list-models, which belongs to the cursor backend, not the subagent one. Subagents can also read the whole workspace, so the 'sees only the files' isolation that the scripts provide isn't enforced for them.
findings.evidence: Line 14: '`subagent` (the default): read-only subagents in this Cursor session.' Line 35: 'A round needs at least two successful reviewers from different model families.' Line 22: 'check it with `cursor-agent --list-models`'. agents/independent-reviewer.md line 4: 'model: inherit'. project.schema.json: approvedReviewBackends 'Defaults to ["subagent"]'.
findings.suggested_fix: Tell the agent to launch each subagent with an explicit model from a different family, or say plainly that the subagent backend can't produce a complete round on its own. For subagents, pass only the artifact contents and tell them not to read other files under upgrade/.

findings.claim: Catch-up runs bootstrap steps 2 and 3 when tracker.csv is missing, without bootstrap's step 1 check. That can overwrite an existing project.json. Later it tells the person to run bootstrap steps 4 to 6, but bootstrap's step 1 and its description stop once a tracker exists, so a model that follows bootstrap from the top halts.
findings.evidence: catch-up line 13: 'If `upgrade/tracker.csv` doesn't exist, run `pg-upgrade-bootstrap` steps 2 and 3'. Line 29: 'run the bootstrap's repo search and approval (bootstrap steps 4 to 6)'. bootstrap line 16: 'If `upgrade/tracker.csv` or `upgrade/project.json` already exists, stop.' bootstrap description: 'Don't use for a migration already in flight'.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the consumer search and approval into a section both skills can call (for example 'Consumer search' in bootstrap, allowed when the tracker exists). Have catch-up merge into an existing project.json rather than rewriting it.

findings.claim: The precheck request fills POSTGRES_<target> from project.json, but the skill doesn't say what to do when target is 'undecided' or 'unknown', or when the source isn't 14. The kit and the reading guide are written for 14 to 18, which pushes the agent to assume 18, against the 'never invent versions' guardrail.
findings.evidence: precheck SKILL.md line 18: '--target-database-version=POSTGRES_<target>'. project.schema.json: target is 'Target major version, "undecided", or "unknown"'. assets/precheck.sql line 3: 'Written for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 14 -> 18.' Section 6a header: 'pg_upgrade 18 refuses from a 14 source'. bootstrap step 7 drafts this request right after approval, when target is often still unknown.
findings.suggested_fix: If target is unknown or undecided, draft the kit-only request, leave the provider precheck as a placeholder plus a Question row, and don't pick a version. If source isn't 14 or target isn't 18, flag the kit sections that are version-specific as possibly not applicable.

findings.claim: The runbook skill fills commands 'from the SOP', but the SOP's Block 2 and 3 commands, timeouts, cancel rule and rollback are Cloud SQL-specific. Unlike the precheck skill, it has no rule for other providers, so on RDS, Azure or self-managed Postgres an agent will either paste gcloud steps or improvise provider commands.
findings.evidence: runbook line 27: 'Fill commands from the SOP with the project's values.' sop.md section 8 lists the Block 2 and 3 parts that are Cloud SQL-only. precheck SKILL.md line 10, by contrast: 'For any other provider ... Mark the provider checks `not supported by this plugin`. Never improvise provider commands.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add the precheck skill's provider rule: when provider isn't cloud-sql, write <placeholder> for every step section 8 lists, add a Question row for each, and never improvise provider commands.

findings.claim: The SOP says the runbook skill drafts a separate logical-path runbook, but the runbook skill has no logical-path instructions and its description doesn't mention it. If the decision record picks DMS, pglogical or pgcopydb, the skill either won't fire or will produce an in-place runbook.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 314: 'If the decision record picks it, the runbook skill drafts a separate logical runbook.' The pg-upgrade-runbook description and sections A to C cover only in-place steps (the analyze branch, new slots after the MVU, the pre-upgrade backup restore). The words 'logical', 'DMS' and 'pgcopydb' don't appear in the skill.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a section to the runbook skill that drafts the logical runbook from SOP section 6, and mention it in the description, or change the SOP so the logical path is flagged as not supported by the plugin.

findings.claim: Several agent-run SOP tasks have no skill, so a request for them fires nothing or the wrong skill: the decision record (B0-12, which gate G0.6 and the review flow depend on), the version research note (B0-10), owner outreach drafts (B0-08), the provider question list (B0-11), census matching (B0-06), and the Block 1 PR shards. Each agent will invent its own format.
findings.evidence: sop.md line 60: 'B0-12 | Decision record | Agent drafts, program owner signs | decision-record.md'. A search of skills/ finds 'decision record' only as an input (runbook line 16, gate-review line 35, model-review line 31). No skill drafts it or defines its sections, even though G0.6 lists about a dozen required fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a decision-record skill or template with the G0.6 fields and their tracker sources. Either add brief skills for B0-06, B0-08, B0-10 and B0-11, or say in the SOP that these are unguided tasks and which existing skill records their output.

findings.claim: Three skills set gate statuses, each with its own rule. Precheck sets a failing G0.2 to 'Waiting on customer', gate-review sets a failing gate to 'Blocked', and runbook part B decides on its own whether G2.x conditions are met. The tracker skill says only gate-review decides whether a gate passes, so the same gate can carry different statuses depending on which skill touched it last.
findings.evidence: gate-review line 32: '`fail`: set the gate to `Blocked`'. precheck line 43: 'If any failed, set it to `Waiting on customer`'. runbook line 45: 'A gate whose condition is met goes to `Needs approval`.' tracker description: 'Don't use to decide whether a gate passes (use pg-upgrade-gate-review).'
findings.suggested_fix: Have precheck and runbook update only their Task and Finding rows and then hand off to gate-review, or define one shared mapping from verdict to gate status that all three cite.

findings.claim: A 'needs decision' verdict means everything is present except a required sign-off. The tracker skill records approval only when the latest report says 'pass'. Neither skill says whether gate-review must run again after the sign-off, so sign-off gates like G0.6 and G2.9 can stall or be closed inconsistently.
findings.evidence: gate-review line 24: '`needs decision`: everything is present, but the SOP needs a named person's sign-off that isn't recorded.' tracker line 28: 'The gate has been through `pg-upgrade-gate-review`, and its latest report says `pass`.'
findings.suggested_fix: Say that a 'needs decision' gate can be recorded Done once the linked sign-off covers the missing item, or that gate-review must run again and return 'pass' first.

findings.claim: Gate-review offers the independent runbook review at Block 3. The runbook is signed off at G1.6 in Block 1, so the review comes after the sign-off it should inform.
findings.evidence: Line 35: 'For Block 0 (the decision record), Block 2 (rehearsal timings) and Block 3 (runbook), suggest `/pg-review`'. sop.md G1.6: 'The program owner and DBA have reviewed the runbook, rollback plan, validation scripts and comms plan'.
findings.suggested_fix: Offer the runbook review at Block 1 (G1.6), and optionally again after Block 2 updates the timings.

findings.claim: Gate-review requires opening every linked piece of evidence, but much of it is a Slack message, a PR review or a CI run that the agent may not be able to reach. The skill doesn't say whether an unreachable link means fail or needs decision, so models will treat it differently.
findings.evidence: Line 16: 'it's `Done` with `Evidence`, and the evidence actually shows its `Done when` (open the linked file or result and confirm)'. tracker line 29 lists approval links as 'a PR review, a signed decision record, or a message URL'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rule: evidence the agent can't open gets the verdict 'needs decision', with the link listed as unverified for a named person to confirm. It's never 'pass'.

findings.claim: The checker treats an unknown owner as covered only when a Question row lists the row's ID in 'Depends on'. No skill says to fill that column, so following the skills literally leaves warnings that different models will resolve differently. The ID format for consumers found from slots or publications is also undefined.
findings.evidence: tracker-lib.mjs line 83 builds questionsFor from Question rows' 'Depends on'. Line 112 warns 'Owner is unknown and no Question row depends on this row'. Running the checker on a Consumer row plus a matching Q-20 whose Notes say 'for C-billing-api' still printed that warning. tracker SKILL.md line 19 says only 'An unknown owner gets a question row.' precheck line 41 adds a Consumer row per unmatched slot without an ID rule (bootstrap uses `C-<repo-name>`).
findings.suggested_fix: State in tracker-schema.md and the tracker skill that the Question row's 'Depends on' must hold the ID of the row it unblocks. Define an ID pattern for slot or publication consumers, such as `C-slot-<slot_name>`.

findings.claim: The workspace-slug rule replaces only '/' and '.', but Cursor also replaces other characters such as '_'. For many paths the computed canvases folder doesn't exist, so the dashboard is never published there and the person gets the fallback link without any warning.
findings.evidence: Line 53: 'The slug is the workspace's absolute path without its leading `/`, with every other `/` and `.` replaced by `-`.' On this machine, workspace '/var/folders/5r/l697v51n5p37v6_0yxw6_4v00000gn/T/pg-review.N45clw' has project folder '~/.cursor/projects/var-folders-5r-l697v51n5p37v6-0yxw6-4v00000gn-T-pg-review-N45clw', where the underscores also became '-'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace every non-alphanumeric character with '-', or list ~/.cursor/projects/ and match the folder, and say when the fallback link is used.

findings.claim: The latest rollback decision time is defined from the window's end, but project.json stores only a duration plus optional free text ('Sunday night'). Models will express it differently (T+minutes or a clock time), and some can't compute it at all. The cutover countdown and the go or no-go owner's approval depend on this one number.
findings.evidence: runbook line 12: 'The latest rollback decision time is the window's end minus 1.25 times the rehearsed end-to-end rollback duration.' project.schema.json window requires only minutes and mode, and 'when' is a free string. bootstrap line 18 example: '"when": "Sunday night"'.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the decision time as T+N minutes from the window start, and show the clock time only when window.when includes a start time and timezone.

findings.claim: The window mode names read the opposite way from their meaning. 'read-write' means both reads and writes stop, and 'write-only' means only writes stop. A bootstrap agent mapping a prompt like 'reads stay up' could easily record the wrong mode.
findings.evidence: Line 25: '"mode": { "enum": ["read-write", "write-only", "unknown"], "description": "read-write: reads and writes both stop; write-only: reads continue" }'.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the values to something like 'full-outage' and 'writes-paused', or 'reads-and-writes-stop' and 'writes-stop'.

findings.claim: The precheck skill tells agents to cite [S-nn] from sources.md, but sources.md has no rows for S-34 to S-37, which the reading guide and SOP cite. In sources.json those four have no status or verified date. S-10 is marked 'changed' but is still used as a plain citation. No skill tells agents to downgrade a claim when its source isn't verified.
findings.evidence: sources.md jumps from S-33 (line 47) to S-40. sources.json defines S-34 to S-37 with only id, title, url, supports and quotes. precheck-reading-guide.md line 53 cites [S-36], and line 51 cites [S-37]. sources.md S-10: 'changed 2026-11-04', and its header says to 'Treat claims that cite it as Unverified until someone rechecks.' Web fetch to recheck S-10 wasn't possible in this run.
findings.suggested_fix: Run check-sources.mjs --write so sources.md covers every ID, and add to the precheck skill and the evidence rule: a source whose status isn't 'verified' makes the claim Unverified.

findings.claim: The provenance check can come out 'unknown' without failing, but G0.2 moves forward only 'if all five passed'. Whether 'unknown' counts as passed isn't stated, so two models can put G0.2 in different statuses from the same paste.
findings.evidence: Line 34: 'Record anything you can't check as `unknown`, without failing on it.' Line 43: 'If all five passed, set G0.2 to `Needs approval` ... If any failed, set it to `Waiting on customer`'.
findings.suggested_fix: Say explicitly whether an 'unknown' provenance result lets G0.2 reach Needs approval, for example 'yes, with the unknown items listed in Notes'.

findings.claim: 'Two levels above' a SKILL.md file can be read as skills/ (the parent of the file's folder) or as the plugin root. Every skill resolves <plugin> this way, and a wrong reading makes the scripts missing, so the agent stops under the rule's own missing-path check.
findings.evidence: Line 28: 'The plugin root is the folder two levels above any of its `SKILL.md` files.' Each skill: '`<plugin>` is the plugin root, two levels above this file'.
findings.suggested_fix: Say '<plugin> is the folder that contains .cursor-plugin/plugin.json (for this file, ../.. relative to the SKILL.md's folder)'.

findings.claim: Bootstrap triggers on and maps values from 'the bootstrap prompt', but no file in the plugin defines that prompt or how its fields map to project.json keys. Its approval step also accepts approval in chat and records it nowhere. The tracker skill rejects chat approvals because the typist can't be verified, and the SOP's Block 0 entry criterion ('repo list approved') then has no evidence.
findings.evidence: bootstrap line 3: 'Set up ... from the bootstrap prompt'. Line 12: 'The bootstrap prompt's values.' A search of review/ finds no bootstrap prompt template; tracker-schema.md only mentions 'the bootstrap prompt's "Tracker" line'. Line 40: 'Don't continue until a named person approves in this conversation.' tracker line 29: 'an approval stated in chat isn't enough.'
findings.suggested_fix: Ship the bootstrap prompt as a template with each field mapped to its project.json key, and record the repo-list approval as a Decision or Task row with the approver and a link (or a note that it was stated in chat).

findings.claim: Daily status posts to Slack 'if the program owner turned that on', but project.json has no opt-in field, so the skill can't tell whether it's on. Step 1 also assumes GitHub or session access to read PR states, with no fallback if that access is missing.
findings.evidence: Line 44: 'A scheduled run ... posts to the project's Slack channel, if the program owner turned that on.' project.schema.json has slackChannel and statusTime but no opt-in flag. Line 36: 'Update statuses from linked PRs and agent sessions.' automations.md: 'nothing sent without the program owner's opt-in.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a field such as slackStatusEnabled (default false) to the schema and check it before posting. If PR state can't be read, leave the row unchanged and list it as 'not checked'.

findings.claim: Statements from people go 'in project.json or a row's Notes' as 'reported by X on date', but project.json fields are typed (for example window.minutes is an integer) and have no place for provenance. Models will either store a reported value as a fact, or invent extra keys.
findings.evidence: Line 18: 'Record each one in `project.json` or a row's `Notes` as "reported by X on date". They're never evidence.' project.schema.json: window.minutes is 'integer', and there's no provenance property.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep reported values out of project.json (leave the field 'unknown') and record them in the Notes of the matching Question row, or add a 'reported' object to the schema with value, by and date.

findings.claim: After approval, bootstrap starts one readiness scan per repo in parallel and links each session. It assumes the agent can launch separate agent sessions (a Project coordinator or cloud agents), and gives no fallback in a plain IDE or CLI session.
findings.evidence: Line 42: 'Start one read-only readiness scan per approved repo, following `<plugin>/reference/readiness-scan.md`, up to `concurrency` at a time. Link each one in `Session or PR`.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add: if separate sessions can't be started, run the scans one at a time in this session, or list them as Not started rows for a person to launch, and leave 'Session or PR' empty.
